prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively name a single “best” lawyer — that depends on your case details and what matters most to you (trial experience, record of big verdicts, communication style, price, language, etc.). I can, however, help you find the right Houston personal injury attorney for a car wreck. A quick plan:

1) Quick questions so I can give a short, tailored list
- What ZIP code or neighborhood are you in? (Houston is big.)
- How serious are the injuries/property damage?
- Was the at-fault driver insured? Were you partially at fault?
- Do you need a Spanish- or other-language lawyer?
- Do you prefer a big firm or a smaller local attorney?

2) How to choose a strong personal injury lawyer
- Relevant experience: handles car wrecks regularly and has trial experience.
- Record: documented settlements/verdicts in similar cases.
- Credentials: board certification in personal injury trial law (if applicable), AV Preeminent or similar peer-review ratings.
- Communication: returns calls, explains strategy, and keeps you updated.
- Team: who will handle the day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?
- Fee structure: contingency fee percentage and who pays costs if you don’t win.
- Local courtroom experience in Harris County courts.

3) Where to look/research
- Texas State Bar lawyer search
- Super Lawyers and Martindale-Hubbell peer-review directories
- Avvo and Google/Yelp client reviews
- Local news articles about large verdicts or settlements
- Referrals from friends, family, or medical providers

4) Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car crash cases like mine have you handled?
- Have you taken similar cases to trial? What were the results?
- Who will actually handle my case day-to-day?
- What percentage is your contingency fee and are there additional costs?
- What’s your estimate of the case value and timeline?
- How will you communicate with me and how often?

5) Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount or outcome
- Reluctance to put fee terms in writing
- Poor responsiveness or evasive answers about experience
- High-pressure “sign now” tactics

6) Practical next steps
- Collect police report, photos, medical bills/records, witness info, insurance details.
- Schedule 2–3 free consultations and compare answers.
- Get the fee agreement in writing before signing.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and a few details about the crash and injuries and I’ll give a short list (3–5) of highly regarded Houston personal injury lawyers or firms you can contact. I can also draft a script or email you can use for the consultations. Which would you prefer?
